item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

## v1.1.0 — OpenTelemetry GenAI support

Ingest GenAI traces from any OpenTelemetry pipeline — no custom SDK required.

**Added**

- New `genai:otel` sourcetype: ingest GenAI traces collected through an

OpenTelemetry Collector. Spans using the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic

conventions (`gen_ai.*`) map to the dashboards automatically.

OpenTelemetry Collector ingestion (`genai:otel`), indexed to `genai_traces`.

**Improved**

- Splunk Cloud compatibility for dashboard and knowledge-object access.

Works with the official OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for OpenAI,

LangChain, LlamaIndex, and more. See the project repository for the collector

configuration and a ready-to-run example.


Short Description:
Observability for LLM, RAG & agent apps. Works with any OpenTelemetry GenAI pipeline — no custom SDK required. Pre-built Splunk dashboards for tokens, latency, cost & errors.


Description:
GenAI Observability for Splunk provides production monitoring for LLM, RAG, and agent applications — track token usage, latency, cost, retrieval quality, and errors across OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, and more. **Works with any OpenTelemetry GenAI pipeline — no custom SDK required.** If you already emit OpenTelemetry GenAI traces (gen_ai.* semantic conventions), point your OpenTelemetry Collector at Splunk and the dashboards light up — with no changes to your application code. Prefer a turnkey setup? An optional lightweight Python SDK instruments your code with simple decorators. Key Features: - Ingests standard OpenTelemetry GenAI traces (gen_ai.* semantic conventions) via the OpenTelemetry Collector - Real-time monitoring of LLM calls, RAG pipelines, and AI agents - Token usage tracking with cost estimation (bundled model-pricing lookup) - Latency analysis with P50, P95, P99 percentiles and tokens/sec - Error detection and alerting - Pre-built dashboards for immediate insights - Optional Python SDK for one-line, decorator-based instrumentation - Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and any OpenTelemetry-instrumented framework Use Cases: - Monitor production AI applications - Optimize token usage and reduce costs - Debug slow or failing LLM calls - Track AI spend by model, workflow, or user - Ensure SLA compliance for AI services Bring your existing OpenTelemetry pipeline, or use the optional SDK — either way you get ready-to-use dashboards, model-pricing lookups, and a collector recipe to get started in minutes. Docs, examples, and the collector configuration: https://github.com/rootiq-ai/splunk_genai_observability/

item.title: Microsoft 365 Defender Threat Vulnerability Add-on for Splunk - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Major release. This version re-architects data collection to run natively inside
Splunk and migrates to Microsoft's current, supported API endpoints. It supersedes the
1.x line, which relied on externally-run Python scripts.

Highlights

  • Native Splunk modular inputs — no external runner required. Data collection is now
    fully self-contained inside the add-on as Splunk modular inputs. Previous versions
    shipped standalone Python scripts that had to run outside Splunk (e.g. a Splunk HF on a
    schedule, or an Azure Function). Credentials, scheduling, and secret management are now
    handled entirely within Splunk.
  • Advanced Hunting migrated to the Microsoft Graph API. CVE description collection
    (ms:defender:vulnerabilities:description) now calls
    https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery, replacing the deprecated
    https://api.security.microsoft.com/api/advancedhunting/run endpoint that Microsoft will
    retire on February 1, 2027.
  • Unified Defender for Endpoint endpoint. The default base URL is now
    https://api.security.microsoft.com (Microsoft's recommended unified endpoint),
    replacing the legacy https://api.securitycenter.microsoft.com.
  • GCC High / DoD login URL corrected. OAuth for GCC High / DoD accounts is now routed
    to https://login.microsoftonline.us instead of https://login.microsoftonline.com.

⚠️ Breaking changes & required actions

  • New API permission required. The Graph migration changes the OAuth token resource to
    https://graph.microsoft.com. Your app registration must hold the
    ThreatHunting.Read.All application permission (replacing AdvancedQuery.Read.All
    under Microsoft Defender for Endpoint). Grant it and obtain admin consent before
    upgrading    , or CVE description collection will fail.
  • External scripts removed. If you previously ran the bundled Python scripts via an HF
    or Azure Function, decommission them after upgrading — collection is now driven by the
    add-on's modular inputs, which you configure on the Inputs tab.

Compatibility notes

  • Both api.security.microsoft.com and the legacy api.securitycenter.microsoft.com
    continue to work; existing account configurations are unaffected by the default
    endpoint change.
  • US GCC and GCC High / DoD Defender endpoints are unchanged (only the GCC High / DoD
    login URL was corrected).


Description:
Vulnerabilities are flaws in a computer system that weakens the overall security of the device or system. And in both small and large organizations it can be quite daunting to keep all devices patched against all vulnerabilities at all times. This is also troublesome for managers, who need to give compliance reports regarding their systems. By utilizing MS Defender Vulnerability framework it is much easier to give a clear answer regarding how well patched your devices are. Import the Defender data to Splunk and give your organization a boost in both threat insights and security analytics. The app comes packaged with one example dashboard to give you an idea of how to use the data. It also CIM normalizes the data into the Vulnerability data model, and holds reports that generates ES ready asset lookups for you. Check out the README for more details.

Short Description:
Monitor SAP security alerts, vulnerabilities, and security notes in Splunk using the Cybersecurity Extension for SAP. Includes 1,200+ detection patterns, real-time sync, and dashboards for Alerts, Vulnerabilities, and Security Notes.


Description:
The Splunk App for the Cybersecurity Extension for SAP (CES) enables security operations teams to monitor, investigate, and respond to SAP security threats directly within Splunk. Integrating SAP security logs with Splunk is challenging due to the complexity of multiple SAP log sources, inconsistent log formats, high raw data volumes, and the lack of predefined SAP-specific detection rules in Splunk. The CES Splunk app addresses these challenges by providing a purpose-built integration that filters, normalises, enriches, and forwards SAP security events to Splunk in real time. The app provides preconfigured dashboards covering three security domains: Alerts, Vulnerabilities, and Security Notes. Alerts are based on more than 1,200 out-of-the-box threat detection patterns applied by CES across SAP systems. Vulnerabilities represent system and user-related security weaknesses detected by CES through daily automated scans using a library of 3,000+ SAP-related checks. Security Notes track relevant, unapplied SAP security patches and their implementation status across systems. Status changes for alerts, vulnerabilities, and security notes are synchronised between CES and Splunk at configurable intervals, ensuring results remain current. Results can be filtered by date, time, system, environment, priority, and status. The app supports deployment via Splunk Universal Forwarder or Syslog and is compatible with Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud.

What's New

  • The configuration tables stay responsive when your `expectedTime` collection holds tens of thousands of rows. Scrolling, sorting, and filtering work smoothly at 25,000+ entries.

item.title: MCP Watch - v1.1.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

MCP-Watch 1.1.0 — multi-signal detection, liveness heartbeats, governance polish

First update since 1.0.0. Three themes: catching custom/community MCPs, real liveness signals, and a CRITICAL alert on data-exfil or data-destroy commands.

NEW

- Multi-signal MCP detection: catches custom / community / non-official MCP servers (no official provenance, generic user-agent) via REST-side user-agent matching + endpoint-based tool inference. New MCP Detection (REST) dashboard, new mcp\_user\_agents.csv lookup. Splunk's reserved identities (admin, splunk-system-user, sidecar\_agent-manager, nobody) are excluded by default via mcp\_excluded\_users.csv.

- Unified MCP Access & Tools dashboard: works whether the official Splunk MCP Server is present (mcp\_tool\_execute capability + tool catalog) or not (RBAC + REST-detected tool usage). Custom MCPs no longer leave the dashboard blank.

- Liveness heartbeats with UP / IDLE / STALE: per-MCP status via mcp\_heartbeat KV collection. Three-state model separates "MCP server down" from "agent idle". Auto-heartbeat for the official Splunk MCP Server when present.

- Getting Started dashboard: in-app onboarding showing current config and live "is data flowing?" checks. Open this first.

- CRITICAL-severity alert "Export or Delete Command Used": captures agent intent to exfil (| outputcsv, | outputlookup, | collect, | sendemail) or destroy (| delete) data. Single hit fires CRITICAL (weight +15).

CHANGED

- "Risky queries %" KPI replaces the unbounded "Risk score" sum (now bounded 0-100, share of MCP queries at MEDIUM band or higher).

- is\_no\_time\_bound weight set to 0 (was 2): MCP servers pass time range as an API parameter, so the flag fired on virtually every query and saturated the score. Still reported in dashboards for transparency.

- REST tool inference covers more endpoints: SAIA tools (saia\_generate\_spl / explain / optimize / ask), validate\_spl, search\_summary, auth\_check.

FIXED

- Phantom MCP agents removed: admin and splunk-system-user no longer appear in detection / access panels (admin role inherits every capability; official server's own housekeeping runs as splunk-system-user with the same user-agent as real traffic).

- Heartbeat scheduled search no longer logs HTTP 404 every 5 minutes when the official MCP Server isn't installed.

- Getting Started Step 1 explains the empty state and shows a helper row on fresh installs.

- Step 2 SPL drops the default placeholder row when editing the user lookup.

- User x Tool matrix no longer errors when no user has the mcp\_tool\_execute capability.

COMPATIBILITY

Splunk Enterprise & Cloud 9.x / 10.x. No restart required.

Reads only built-in \_audit / \_internal — no ingestion, no CIM, no companion app needed.


Short Description:
Tracks AI agent activity in Splunk by analyzing _audit and _internal logs to surface MCP server queries, flag anti-patterns, and report REST endpoint usage.


Description:
MCP-Watch provides visibility and governance for AI agents operating against Splunk through the Model Context Protocol. The app surfaces every SPL query executed by MCP servers, flags anti-patterns such as wildcard index searches and overly wide time ranges, and reports on REST endpoint usage. It reads exclusively from Splunk's built-in _audit and _internal indexes, requiring no additional data ingestion or dependencies. Administrators configure a lookup table with the Splunk usernames their MCP servers authenticate as, and the app then tracks query volume, identifies quality issues, and enables per-user tool access governance. item.title: AI Workbench - v1.3.2 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Release notes — AI Assistent for Splunk

This file tracks every customer-visible change.

Format: Keep a Changelog. Dates
are ISO-8601. App version in default/app.conf always matches the
top entry.

Versioning note (2026-06). Releases formerly numbered 0.10.0–0.13.0
were renumbered to 1.0.0–1.3.0 to reflect production maturity — the app
had been stable and feature-complete across SPL, dashboards, ML, ES/ITSI,
tenancy, the skills layer, the knowledge layer, reliability/observability,
SSE content, and real audit logging well before the cosmetic 0.x. The
mapping is exact: 0.10.0 → 1.0.0, 0.11.0 → 1.1.0, 0.11.1 → 1.1.1,
0.12.0 → 1.2.0, 0.13.0 → 1.3.0. The 0.9.x and earlier entries below
are pre-1.0 history and keep their original numbers. The planned data-
foundation and platform-ops releases are now 1.4.0 and 1.5.0
(see docs/ROADMAP_AND_VISION.md). No code or behaviour changed in the
renumbering — only version strings, headers, and "introduced-in" references.

1.3.2 — 2026-06-03

First Splunkbase 1.x publish — packaging hygiene + KVStore ACL completeness.
Carries everything in 1.3.1 (token-cost cuts, knowledge-unlocks-tools, TrackMe
+ audit + Org/BU fixes); this entry adds the release-readiness changes.

Fixed

  • trackme_health_for_indexes now actually finds tracked indexes (was
    always not_tracked).     The tool called TrackMe v2 endpoints that do not
    exist     — trackme/v2/tenants/list_tenants and
    trackme/v2/data_source/get_entities — which 404'd and were swallowed, so
    every index came back not_tracked even when TrackMe was clearly tracking it
    (e.g. _internal with 100+ entities under the dutchdatadifference tenant).
    It now uses the real API: GET trackme/v2/vtenants/show_tenants for the
    tenant list and POST trackme/v2/splk_dsm/dsm_get_table (JSON under the
    payload form field) per tenant, parses the plain-array responses, matches on
    the entity's data_index field (robust to any index / index:sourcetype /
    index:sourcetype:source DSM split — with a first-segment-of-object
    fallback), and reads the correct status field object_state. The result is
    now a token-cheap summary — verdict + entity_count + per-status counts +
    tracking tenants + a worst-first capped sample — instead of dumping every
    entity. After live testing showed the custom trackme/v2 handlers can return
    an empty body through the splunkweb browser proxy (the tenant list came
    back empty, so every index was still falsely not_tracked),
    trackme_health_for_indexes — plus trackme_list_tenants and
    trackme_list_entities — now read TrackMe's KVStore collections directly
    via the core storage/collections/data endpoint
    (kv_trackme_virtual_tenants, kv_trackme_<comp>_tenant_<tenant>), which
    proxies reliably and returns clean records, with the index filter pushed into
    the KVStore query. Verified live: _internal now resolves as tracked with
    its real green/red counts. (src/services/tools.ts.)
  • The generated TrackMe dashboard panel now works (and stops claiming
    "TrackMe does not monitor this index").     The feed-health-verdict skill's
    panel recipe pointed at the wrong collection name (missing the kv_ prefix),
    the wrong status field (coalesce(state,status) instead of object_state),
    and produced no rows (TrackMe's | trackme / KVStore reads return the whole
    result as one JSON event, so search/stats silently did nothing — which is
    why the assistant gave up and wrote a misleading "not monitored" note). The
    skill now leads with a plain TrackMe summary-index search (live-verified
    against the running instance) — trackme_health_for_indexes returns the
    tenant's summary_index plus ready-made panel_spl_trend
    (index=<summary> object=<index>* object_state=* | timechart span=5m count by object_state) and panel_spl_current (latest state per object → counts), so
    the panel is a normal index search with no KVStore read, no inputlookup, no
    | trackme/spath. (The | trackme … dsm_get_table | spath | mvexpand route
    is kept as a documented fallback.) The skill also tells the model never to
    claim an index is unmonitored unless trackme_health_for_indexes returned
    tracked:false. The always-applied dashboard-xml-discipline skill carries
    the same HARD rule (never inputlookup trackme_*, never invent a lookup name
    like trackme_dsm_idx_summary). trackme_health_for_indexes also returns
    three ready-to-paste, live-verified panel SPLs — panel_spl_summary
    (one panel: per-state counts + total + a readable string, using count AS total_feeds NOT count(*)), panel_spl_trend (timechart), and
    panel_spl_red_table (red-feed detail) — so the model pastes a working panel
    instead of composing one. The same canonical recipe is registered as a
    curated knowledge entry (trackme-feed-health-dashboard-panel-recipe,
    assigned_tools: [trackme_health_for_indexes]) so it's retrievable via the
    knowledge layer — the exact-search-as-data pattern. Finally the dashboard
    validator     now appends actionable fix-hints for three recurring failures so
    the self-correct loop fixes them deterministically (bundle-level, no skill
    reseed needed): inputlookup trackme_*; a stats rename with a * wildcard
    ("number of wildcards … do not match"); and a malformed where from the
    field=$token$ OR "*"="*" multiselect-filter idiom (bare field=* is invalid
    in where — filter in the base search via | search field=$token$ instead).
    (src/services/skillSeeds.ts, src/services/tools.ts,
    bin/knowledge_seeds.py.)
  • The entire TrackMe tool suite now hits real endpoints. Every other
    trackme_* tool was calling invented v2 paths that 404'd. All were rewritten
    against TrackMe's actual handlers (verified from the handler source):
    trackme_list_tenants/get_tenant → vtenants/show_tenants/show_tenant;
    trackme_list_entities/get_entity/get_identity_card → the per-component
    table + <short>_entity_info (dsm_get_table, ds_entity_info, …, with the
    inconsistent short prefix dsm→ds/dhm→dh/mhm→mh/wlk→wlk handled centrally);
    trackme_smart_status → splk_smart_status/<short>_smart_status (trimmed to
    the verdict); trackme_get_workload_status/get_search_perf →
    splk_wlk/wlk_get_table/wlk_entity_info; trackme_list_acks →
    ack/get_ack_for_object; trackme_ack_entity → ack/write/ack_manage
    (ack_period in seconds); trackme_list_maintenance/update_maintenance
    → the per-tenant/global maintenance endpoints (maintenance is NOT
    per-entity — the tool signature changed accordingly);
    trackme_update_entity_priority → splk_<comp>/write/<short>_update_priority
    with the correct named-tier values low/medium/high/critical/pending
    (was wrongly validating P1/P2/P3); trackme_get_outliers →
    splk_outliers_engine/outliers_get_data; trackme_get_version →
    configuration/request_info. All POSTs now send JSON under the payload
    form field and parse the plain-array/object responses via shared helpers.
    Two tools were honestly down-scoped: CIM compliance has no per-entity REST
    endpoint in this TrackMe version, so trackme_get_cim_compliance /
    trackme_list_cim_issues now return the tenant-level CIM summary with a clear
    note; trackme_get_entity_metrics returns the entity's deployment-correct
    mstats/timechart SPL templates (TrackMe metrics live in a metric index) rather
    than guessing measure names. (src/services/tools.ts.)
  • Ask no longer fails with A maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control may be provided. Found 5. The 1.3.1 prompt-caching change marked a cache_control
    breakpoint on the last message block, but it mutated the shared message
    content in place     — and the dispatcher reuses one growing messages array
    across every tool-loop turn, so each turn left a stale breakpoint on a prior
    block. After three tool turns the count reached 5 and Anthropic rejected the
    request (HTTP 400), breaking any multi-step Ask (e.g. the Simple XML dashboard
    template). The adapter now clones the last message before marking it, so
    cache_control never persists onto earlier turns and the breakpoint count is
    a deterministic 3 (system + last tool + last message) every call.
    (src/services/llm/anthropic_adapter.ts.)
  • Every KVStore collection now ships an explicit ACL. Seven collections —
    the three knowledge collections (itmip_ai_knowledge_entries,
    itmip_knowledge_connectors, itmip_knowledge_static_rules), the two MCP
    collections (itmip_mcp_servers, itmip_mcp_tools), itmip_tool_overrides,
    and the internal itmip_kvstore_restore_lock — had no stanza in
    metadata/default.meta     and silently inherited the global default
    (write: [admin, sc_admin, power], export = system). They now carry
    explicit stanzas matching the app's uniform convention: writes are
    admin-only     (authoring / configuration is an admin act) and export = none (app-scoped, like every other collection). This does not change
    what user / power roles can do — the React shell reaches collections via
    an explicit /servicesNS/nobody/<app>/ path (where export governs cross-app
    visibility, not role access), and normal users reach the knowledge / MCP
    data only through system-token REST handlers. Read stays open on the content
    collections (knowledge, tool-overrides, MCP tool defs) so nothing end-user is
    blocked; itmip_mcp_servers (which carries endpoint + auth references) is
    read-scoped to admin / sc_admin / power like itmip_llm_configs. The
    knowledge REST handler also gets an explicit read: [*] / export = system
    stanza so the Ask flow can always invoke it. (metadata/default.meta.)
  • Dev-only scripts/*.ts no longer ships in the .spl. git archive
    was packaging scripts/snapshot_prompts.ts (a build/diagnostic helper never
    loaded by Splunk at runtime). Added scripts/ export-ignore so the tarball
    carries only Splunk app content. (.gitattributes.)

Changed

  • Docs: docs/PACKAGING.md refreshed to 1.3.2 — corrected the tarball
    file count and size, and added the knowledge-layer handlers + connectors and
    the knowledge-health view to the "what the tarball contains" table.

1.3.1 — 2026-06-03

Bug fixes — Org/BU editing data loss, and a seed-drift guard.

Fixed

  • Editing an Organisation or Business Unit no longer drops its identity.
    The tenancy update path wrote a partial record, and a Splunk KVStore
    POST to an existing _key replaces the whole record — so each Org
    edit silently dropped the immutable short (and created_at), and each BU
    edit dropped short and org_short (breaking the BU's tenant linkage).
    A row whose short had been blanked then rendered a blank, disabled Short
    field and could not be saved (the Save button is disabled / validation
    rejects an empty short) — most visibly when re-editing the DFLT Org
    after configuring audit logging. The update now merges onto the existing
    row and pins the identity, and self-heals an already-blanked row from
    its _key on the next save. The Org/BU editors and list also fall back to
    the _key so a blanked row still shows its identity and can be saved.
    (bin/itmip_llm_tenancy.py, src/components/OrgsBusPage.tsx,
    src/services/tenancyAdmin.ts.)
  • Ask no longer fails with "tools: Tool names must be unique." The tool
    list sent to the LLM is the union of built-ins + custom HTTP tools +
    MCP-imported tools and was not de-duplicated, so a custom/MCP tool whose
    name collided with a built-in (or the same tool imported from two MCP
    servers) made the provider reject the entire request. The assembled list is
    now de-duplicated by name, keeping the built-in (a custom/MCP tool cannot
    shadow a built-in name). (src/services/llm/ask.ts.)
  • Audit tab — selecting an Org with a configured index works again. The
    Org picker keyed options on short; when two Orgs had a blank/duplicate
    short (a symptom of the data-loss bug above) they collapsed into one
    un-selectable entry, so an Org like TDDD couldn't be chosen even though its
    index was set. The picker now keys on the unique _key.
    (src/components/AuditPage.tsx.)
  • Audit logging now works for Orgs whose short was blanked, and the
    resolved Org shows correctly (no more Org: •).     The server-side tenant
    resolver and the audit-config lookup matched Orgs/BUs by short only — so a
    row blanked by the data-loss bug resolved to an empty org_short, which
    meant the per-Org audit index couldn't be found and nothing was logged
    (and the header read Org: •). Both now fall back to the _key (which is
    the Org short), and BUs recover org_short/short from the composite _key.
    (bin/itmip_llm_common.py, bin/itmip_llm_audit.py.)
  • TrackMe tools work again (were 404 / "not_tracked" even when TrackMe had
    data).     Every trackme_* tool called TrackMe's trackme/v2/... REST API
    via the bare /services/... path, but those endpoints are registered under
    /servicesNS/<user>/trackme/... — so trackme_list_tenants 404'd,
    trackme_list_entities returned "'/services' is not supported", and
    trackme_health_for_indexes therefore saw zero tenants and reported

    against the stripped sub-segment; on this Splunk version the
    sub-path arrives with the match-prefix included, so every call
    was 404'ing. Switched to substring matching
    ("user_create" in path) to mirror the proven
    bin/itmip_llm_mcp.py pattern.
  2. KVStore POST _key extraction — _post() to KVStore omitted
    ?output_mode=json, so the response came back as XML and the
    _key from json.loads(content) was always empty in the
    dispatcher envelope. Added ?output_mode=json +
    getargs={"output_mode": "json"} + rawResult=True matching
    the MCP handler.
  3. Forbidden-content regex false positives — the role-elevation
    pattern \bset\s+(my|your|the)\s+role\s+to\b matched legitimate
    English ("Set my role to investigate this further"). Tightened
    to require an admin-equivalent target role
    (admin|sc_admin|power|splunk_admin).
  4. Forbidden-content scan was soft. The scan only logged
    matches to attempted_override_fields[] and persisted the
    template anyway. Per spec §4.2 step 6 (body MUST NOT contain ...)
    the scan now adds to errors[] and hard-rejects, so the
    workflow retry loop self-corrects.
  5. Error envelope shape — err(status, {...}) wrapped the body
    under {"error": ...} but the dispatcher reads top-level
    {ok, errors[]}. Worse, the TS splunkFetch throws on non-2xx
    before the dispatcher can read the body, so the LLM saw
    "Splunk REST POST failed: 400" with no detail. Introduced an
    envelope() helper that returns 200 + {ok: false, errors: [...]}
    for validation / quota / ownership failures (the LLM can read
    and self-correct); real 4xx/5xx is reserved for "dispatcher is
    broken" cases (missing auth, KVStore down).

Backup robustness

  • itmip_authoring_changes 404 on fresh installs. Splunk's KVStore
    materialises a collection lazily on first write; on installs where
    no end user has authored a template yet, the new audit collection
    doesn't exist physically and splunk.rest.simpleRequest() raises
    splunk.RESTException with [HTTP 404] <url>. The backup script
    now catches the exception, parses the embedded status code, and
    treats 404 as an empty collection — same semantics as the original
    non-raising branch. Same defence applied to
    bin/itmip_llm_skills.py so a fresh install where itmip_ai_skills
    hasn't been seeded yet falls back to the in-bundle seed catalogue
    cleanly.
  • 503 retry on KVStore startup. _list_collection_rows() in
    bin/itmip_llm_kvstore_backup.py now retries up to 3 times with
    2 / 4 second backoff on 503, which handles the
    ~10-second window after every splunk restart when Mongo is
    warming up. Previously a single transient 503 would fail all 13
    collections in one backup run.
  • Better backup error messages. Non-2xx responses now include
    the first 500 chars of splunkd's response body in the error
    string, so the operator can see exactly why a request was
    refused. Common 503 causes (KVStore disabled, Mongo migration in
    progress, SHC captain re-election) are named in the docstring so

server is authoritative: any value the LLM emits for
sharing / owner_user / creator / required_roles /
dependent_apps / is_default / is_general / status is silently
overridden and logged.

Security model (recap)

Custom tools are a powerful primitive — admins can wire the LLM up
to any HTTP API in the organisation. The release is designed so the
blast radius of a mistake or a compromised admin account is bounded:

  • Tool definitions can only be written by admins. End users see them
    in the LLM's tool list but cannot edit.
  • Secrets live in storage/passwords and are resolved server-side
    on every call. The definition can be exported and shared safely —
    the secret stays per-environment.
  • allowed_hosts is a per-tool allowlist enforced after template
    substitution so a parameter-driven URL can't reach an unintended
    host (SSRF defence).
  • RFC1918 and loopback hosts are refused by default — admins must
    set allow_internal: true to wire up internal-network tools.
  • Every invocation is audited with the calling user, the tool, a
    hash of the arguments, the outcome, and the duration.

  "version": "1.0.0",
  "title": "Get ServiceNow Incident",
  "description": "Fetches a ServiceNow incident by number (e.g. INC0012345). Use this when the user asks about a specific incident, or when correlating a Splunk alert to an ITSM ticket.",
  "scope": { "sharing": "app", "owner_org": "ACME", "owner_bu": "SECOPS" },
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "incident_number": {
        "type": "string",
        "pattern": "^INC[0-9]{7}$",
        "description": "ServiceNow incident number"
      }
    },
    "required": ["incident_number"]
  },
  "implementation": {
    "type": "http",
    "method": "GET",
    "url": "https://acme.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident",
    "query": { "sysparm_query": "number={{ incident_number }}" },
    "auth": { "type": "basic", "credential_ref": "servicenow_readonly", "username": "splunk_ai" },
    "timeout_seconds": 10,
    "allowed_hosts": ["acme.service-now.com"]
  },
  "response": {
    "transform": "jq",
    "expression": ".result[0] | {number, summary: .short_description, state}",
    "max_bytes": 8192
  },

  • Removing every recipient email left a dead alert behind. Now
    saving an empty recipient list deletes the saved alert outright
    instead of leaving one that fires and emails no one.
  • make spl packaging deleted the React bundle after it finished
    archiving (a side effect of force-adding appserver/static/build/
    on a temp branch + git checkout - to the original branch). The
    Makefile now re-runs npm run build at the very end so the local
    Splunk install stays in a runnable state after every packaging run.
  • Makefile was being shipped in the .spl, tripping AppInspect's
    check_destructive_commands on its dev-cleanup rm -rf
    instructions. Added Makefile export-ignore to .gitattributes
    and switched git archive to --worktree-attributes so the
    exclusion takes effect without needing a commit first.
  • AI Toolkit dashboards generated from outside the Splunk_ML_Toolkit
    app threw "Failed to load model — Model does not exist".     The
    template flow now pins the training + scoring saved searches to
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit + global sharing, then explicitly promotes the
    model file so apply resolves from any calling app.
  • MIME-type / 404 errors at the React shell when
    appserver/static/build/main.js was missing post-rename or
    post-make spl. Documented in
    tasks/lessons.md and now self-healing via the
    Makefile fix above.
  • CSRF silent fallback in splunkFetch removed — state-changing
    requests now throw a clear SplunkApiError(status=0) when the
    token cookie is missing, instead of degrading to an unauthenticated
    request that splunkd will reject far downstream.

Security

  • All 5 BLOCKER + 9 HIGH findings from the v0.2.x audit are
    resolved.     Highlights:
  • /services/itmip_llm/secret POST/DELETE now requires admin
    server-side; GET is rate-limited and gated on per-LLM allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/proxy no longer accepts caller-supplied
    endpoint; uses the stored LlmConfig.endpoint. Caller-supplied
    extra_headers filtered against a 3-entry allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/api_key admin-only; bootstrap LLM defaults
    to splunk_proxy so the key stays on the SH.
  • KVStore collection ACLs for itmip_llm_configs,
    itmip_organisations, itmip_business_units,
    itmip_tool_assignments, itmip_llm_license tightened to
    read/write: [admin, power / sc_admin].
  • SPL injection guard: rejectSideEffectSpl() runs inside every
    LLM-dispatched search and refuses outputlookup, outputcsv,
    sendemail, sendalert, collect, summaryindex, tscollect,
    metasearch, script, runshellscript, delete.
  • Dashboard XML lint refuses <script>, <iframe>, <object>,
    <embed>, javascript: URLs, inline event handlers.
  • Per-user rate limits added to the most-spammable endpoints (30/min
    on secret GET + proxy, 120/min on usage_log).
  • The full status board is in docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md.

Removed

  • Legacy v0.1 "Anthropic API key" card under Settings. The
    storage path (storage/passwords realm = itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app,
    name = anthropic_api_key) is still read transparently by
    loadSecretForConfig() as a fallback for the bootstrap LLM, so
    existing installs that pre-date the rename keep working.

Known limitations

  • Concurrent-session enforcement on the Personal tier is UI-only —
    cross-browser hard enforcement needs a heartbeat protocol.
  • The Cryptolens product access token is embedded in code (this is
    the vendor-recommended pattern — it is the product's read-only
    API key, not a customer secret). A scanner may flag it; document
    the rationale on Splunkbase submission if asked.

0.2.x — internal release stream

A series of internal iterations between 2026-03 and 2026-05-12 leading
up to 0.3.0. Highlights worth knowing if you're upgrading from a
pre-0.3.0 build:

Added (during 0.2.x)

  • Multi-LLM support: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Gemini,
    Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Pick provider + model per LLM
    configuration.
  • Two call modes per LLM: browser_direct (lowest latency,
    CORS-limited) and splunk_proxy (works everywhere, keys
    server-side).
  • Streaming responses for Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible providers.
  • Multi-tenant Organisations + Business Units. Templates and LLM
    configs scope per Org/BU. Resolved per page load from the user's
    Splunk app + role.
  • Use-case templates for SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards,
    Dashboard Studio JSON, alerts (with companion dashboards), saved
    searches, reports, lookups, field extractions, plus 10 Splunk AI
    Toolkit pipelines.
  • Tokens & Costs tab — multi-axis side-by-side cost analytics
    (App / User / Model / Provider / Org / BU / LLM config) over time.
  • Tools tab — per-Org/BU enable/disable of every LLM tool.
  • TLS CA certificate (PEM) upload per LLM (server-side proxy
    honours customer-internal CAs).
  • Extra HTTP headers per LLM (static tokens, customer-internal
    gateway headers).
  • KVStore-backed user history with per-question template / LLM /
    provider / model / token / cost attribution and clickable links to
    every created knowledge object.

Renamed (during 0.2.x)

  • App id stayed itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app; label evolved from
    "Claude Assistant for Splunk" → "AI User Assistent for Splunk" →
    (in 0.3.0) "AI Assistent for Splunk".
  • All bin/itmip_claude_*.py Python handlers renamed to
    bin/itmip_llm_*.py. Legacy URLs (/services/itmip_claude/*)
    retired; new ones live under /services/itmip_llm/*.

0.1.x — pre-history

The original "Claude Assistant for Splunk" with a single Anthropic
provider and a hand-stored API key under storage/passwords realm =
itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app, name = anthropic_api_key. The
legacy key path is still readable by the bootstrap LLM in 0.3.x for
backward compatibility — no migration step needed.


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
AI Workbench is a generative workspace for Splunk. Not a chatbot bolted onto search but a real workbench, where you investigate, analyse and build using tools that understand Splunk natively. The Workbench is built as a host shell. It has no use-cases of its own — it derives everything from the Splunk app a user opens it from and the Splunk roles they hold. Install it once on the Search Head, then embed it into the apps your users already live in: Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC apps, your MSP customer apps. The same engine renders a different experience per calling app, with different templates, different LLMs, different tools, and writes its outputs into that calling app's namespace. End users never leave the app they came from. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and Splunk AI Toolkit (MLTK) pipelines. Every artefact is run for real before it is saved, and every artefact is a normal Splunk knowledge object — owned by the calling user, in the calling app, findable in Splunk's own UI. The depth is the difference. Where a generic MCP-only assistant talks to Splunk through one broad door, AI Workbench ships with fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe and the AI Toolkit — roughly fifty of them, each scoped to one job a Splunk admin actually does. The LLM picks the right tool for the question, runs it under your existing Splunk ACLs, and shows its work. Extend it further by adding HTTP tools or registering any MCP server in the Tools tab. Two audiences benefit immediately. Splunk users who know what they want but find SPL foreign get production-quality searches and dashboards generated and validated panel-by-panel. Splunk users who bounce off MLTK get an outlier detector, forecaster, classifier or clusterer built end-to-end, with a companion dashboard that proves the model is doing something sensible. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama (local, fully offline) or OpenRouter. Browser-direct for speed, or Splunk-server-side proxy mode so API keys never leave the search head. Bring your own corporate IAM — WebEAM.Next, Ping, Okta, AzureAD, internal SAML — via a customer-supplied Python hook that mints fresh auth headers per request. Multi-tenant by design. Organisations and Business Units are resolved automatically from the calling app and the user's roles — end users don't pick a tenant. Templates, LLM configurations and tool availability all scope per Org or BU. Run one Splunk environment for many teams or many customers without them seeing each other. Tokens and Costs breaks spend down by App, User, Model, Provider, Organisation, BU or LLM configuration — over time, with real per-model pricing. Free, Professional, Enterprise and MSP licence tiers, activated self-serve, air-gap-friendly.

item.title: LegacyTel - vnull [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
LegacyTel is a zero-dependency, high-performance Go-based log normalization gateway designed to bridge the gap between legacy core infrastructure (IBM z/OS Mainframe SMF, IBM i AS/400 QAUDJRN, HPE NonStop EMS) and Splunk. It securely ingests, decodes CP1047 EBCDIC, and maps native legacy security events directly into standard, Splunk CIM-compliant structures.


Description:
The LegacyTel Add-on for Splunk addresses one of the most critical and costly blind spots in modern Security Operations Centers (SOCs): the lack of visibility into legacy core transaction systems. Mainframes and midrange platforms (IBM z/OS, IBM i Series/AS400, and HPE NonStop Tandem) run the vast majority of global core transactional workloads. However, their operational and audit logs—such as SMF, QAUDJRN, and EMS records—remain highly siloed. They are written in complex binary formats and EBCDIC (Code Page 1047) character encodings that modern security pipelines cannot read. Traditionally, onboarding these logs required heavy, expensive, proprietary proprietary agents that added high compute overhead to production environments. LegacyTel solves this challenge natively as an open-source, ultra-lightweight observability gateway written in pure Go (standard-library only). Purpose & Capabilities: - Ingests native, raw event streams from z/OS SMF, IBM i QAUDJRN, and HPE NonStop EMS over secure TCP sockets. - Translates character encodings instantly using an optimized, zero-allocation CP1047 EBCDIC-to-ASCII translation table. - Normalizes disparate legacy schemas into a unified, standard compliance taxonomy (such as LL01-CM04 codes for login, configuration, and privilege modifications). - Decouples core legacy performance from Splunk latency using an asynchronous, buffered concurrent pipeline. - Fully secures data in transit over internal networks utilizing TLS 1.2/tls 1.3 and Mutual TLS (mTLS) with client certificate verification. - Packages parsing, field extraction, and Common Information Model (CIM) configurations (Props/Transforms) to ensure all legacy logs instantly map to standard Splunk datasets (e.g. Authentication, Change, and Performance). By normalizing logs at the ingest layer and providing pre-built CIM mapping configurations, the LegacyTel Add-on for Splunk enables organizations to establish a unified, real-time security posture across legacy and cloud environments without high compute overhead or expensive proprietary forwarders.

Initial release of TA - Splunk UF Upgrade Automation for Windows.

This release provides the endpoint-side automation component for controlled Windows Universal Forwarder upgrade workflows.

Added

  • Windows Universal Forwarder upgrade automation for targeted Windows endpoints.
  • MSI installer discovery from the local splunk_installer directory.
  • MSI filename validation and target version extraction.
  • Current Splunk Universal Forwarder version validation.
  • Upgrade path validation to help prevent unsupported upgrade attempts.

  • Persistent JSON state tracking under C:\ProgramData\SplunkUpgrade\state\.
  • Retry-loop prevention for previously attempted MSI installers.
  • Controlled force retry support for selected failed endpoints.
  • Retry marker reset support for preparing selected endpoints for another retry wave.
  • Event code coverage for setup, validation, scheduled task, service control, upgrade result, cleanup, state tracking, retry prevention, force retry, and retry reset activity.

Supported Companion Apps

This app is designed to work with:

App Purpose
TA-windows_uf_upgrade_parsing Provides index and sourcetype parsing support for upgrade logs and MSI installer logs.
SA-windows_uf_upgrade_monitoring Provides dashboards, reporting views, data model support, and troubleshooting workflows.

Important Notes

  • This TA performs endpoint-side operational actions on Windows Universal Forwarders.
  • All inputs are disabled by default and should be enabled intentionally through Deployment Server server classes, local overrides, or approved configuration management.
  • The main upgrade scripted input should be enabled only when the target endpoints and MSI package are ready.
  • The force retry input should be enabled only for selected failed endpoints after the underlying issue has been reviewed and fixed.
  • The retry reset input should be enabled only when preparing selected endpoints for another retry wave.

Known Considerations

  • The splunk_upgrade index must exist before endpoint logs can be indexed successfully.
  • TA-windows_uf_upgrade_parsing should be deployed to the parsing/indexing tier before enabling log collection at scale.
  • MSI log collection can generate verbose data and should be enabled according to troubleshooting, audit, and retention needs.
  • The app expects the Splunk Universal Forwarder to be installed in the default path unless script variables are adjusted.
  • The staged MSI filename must contain a parseable target version.
  • A failed upgrade may be intentionally skipped on later runs if the same MSI hash is marked do_not_retry=true.
  • Controlled retry should be used instead of manually deleting state files when retrying failed endpoints at scale.


Short Description:
Automates Windows Universal Forwarder upgrades with MSI validation, scheduled task execution, upgrade logging, state tracking, retry-loop prevention, and controlled retry/reset support.


Description:
TA - Splunk UF Upgrade Automation for Windows is the endpoint-side automation component for controlled Windows Universal Forwarder upgrade workflows. This TA is deployed to Windows Universal Forwarders and can validate staged Splunk Universal Forwarder MSI installers, check installed and target versions, create and start a Windows Scheduled Task, execute the upgrade process, stop and start the Splunk Universal Forwarder service, write upgrade logs, and track local JSON state. The app is designed to help administrators perform safer upgrade rollouts by preventing uncontrolled retry loops against the same MSI installer. If an installer has already reached a terminal state, the app can skip repeated attempts and log retry-prevention activity. When a retry is intentionally needed, the TA also includes controlled force retry and retry reset logic that can be enabled only for selected endpoints. All inputs are disabled by default for safety. Administrators should enable only the required inputs through Deployment Server server classes, local overrides, or approved configuration management. This TA works with the companion parsing app TA-windows_uf_upgrade_parsing, which provides index and sourcetype parsing support, and the optional monitoring app SA-windows_uf_upgrade_monitoring, which provides dashboards, reporting views, and troubleshooting workflows. Description:
**UK Open Data** is a UCC-framework built add-on that brings two well-known open UK datasets into Splunk with no API key and no external dependencies beyond outbound HTTPS. **Carbon Intensity** — polls the National Grid ESO Carbon Intensity API (`api.carbonintensity.org.uk`) and indexes, per half-hourly settlement period, the national forecast/actual gCO₂/kWh and intensity band (`carbonintensity:national`) plus the generation mix by fuel type (`carbonintensity:generation`). Ideal for carbon-aware scheduling, ESG dashboards and "greenest time to run" decisions. **NHS A&E (monthly)** — scans the NHS England "A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions" pages, downloads each monthly CSV you haven't already loaded, and indexes one event per provider plus a national TOTAL row (`nhs:ae:monthly`) — type 1/2/other attendances, 4-hour performance and over-4hr counts. Great for healthcare performance and public-sector analytics. Both inputs are **idempotent**: they checkpoint what they've already indexed, so they're safe to run on any interval without creating duplicates. Carbon re-emits only un-settled recent periods until their actual value lands; NHS only loads months it hasn't seen. Built with the Splunk UCC framework — full configuration UI, per-input index/interval settings, and standard logging.

Release Notes:

AI Query Assistant for Splunk — v4.0.2

v4.0.2 is a security and license stability hardening release.

AI capabilities, Agentic Pipeline behavior, Provider configuration, and query behavior are unchanged from v4.0.1. Existing 4.x licenses continue to work after upgrade, with no license re-issuance required.

WHAT'S NEW

  • Enhanced local license validation to detect modified or invalid license files, including offline environments.
  • Improved license protection when the license server is temporarily unavailable.
  • Stronger consistency checks between the license and the current runtime environment.
  • Improved isolation between different licenses and license states.
  • More reliable license status handling for enterprise deployment scenarios.

HARDENING FIXES

  • Removed a development-only configuration path from release builds.
  • Fixed scenarios where license state could be reused unexpectedly.
  • Improved license state isolation in multi-license and multi-environment scenarios.
  • Strengthened offline license validation behavior.

COMPATIBILITY

  • Splunk Enterprise 10.0+: Basic NL-to-SPL query capability.
  • Splunk Enterprise 10.2+: Agentic Pipeline capability.
  • Splunk Enterprise 10.4+: Full Agentic query path enabled by default.

UPGRADE FROM 4.0.1

In-place upgrade is supported. No data migration or license re-issuance is required.

  1. Install the new app package from Splunkbase or run:
splunk install app ... -update 1
  1. Install or update runtime dependencies:
python bin/install_deps.py
  1. Restart Splunk and confirm that the existing license is still active.

ROLLBACK

Rollback to v4.0.1 is safe. v4.0.2 uses the same data formats and license compatibility as v4.0.0.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS

  • Splunk 10.0 and 10.1 support only the basic NL-to-SPL query capability.
  • The full Agentic Pipeline requires Splunk 10.2 or later.
  • First-time dependency installation downloads approximately 150 MB of runtime packages.

SUPPORT
